# CI

**There is intentionally no CI in this repository right now.**

Dalaran inherited ~54 GitHub Actions workflows from upstream Rerun, all wired to
infrastructure this project does not have (private GCS buckets, self-hosted
runner pools, Slack/analytics hooks, upstream release orchestration). Those were
removed. A lean replacement set was then trialled and also removed: it produced
failing checks on every push for reasons that have nothing to do with whether
the code is good, which is worse than no signal at all.

## Why the replacement set was pulled

- **`cargo check --workspace`** — the workspace contains the `dalaran_py` pyo3
  extension, which requires a `PYO3_CONFIG_FILE` generated by the pixi
  environment (`pixi run ensure-pyo3-build-cfg`). Without it the build fails at
  `pyo3-build-config`. A hosted runner would need the full pixi bootstrap first.
- **Python wheel / mypy** — the wheel job needs that same native build, and mypy
  surfaced pre-existing strictness gaps across the tree.
- **C++ / docs** — both need a full Arrow build or a built SDK, which is slow and
  fragile on free runners.

None of these are correctness problems in the merged code. Verification is done
locally instead (see below).

## How to verify a change without CI

```sh
# Rust: builds clean, zero warnings
export PROTOC=$(which protoc)
cargo check --workspace --all-features
cargo fmt --all --check

# Python: pure-Python packages need no native build
python3 -m pytest dalaran_py/tests/unit/ros2 dalaran_py/tests/unit/tools \
                 dalaran_py/tests/unit/test_robot_*.py -q
ruff check . && ruff format --check .
```

For the full environment (native bindings, C++ SDK, docs site) use pixi:
`pixi run check-env`, `pixi run py-build`, `pixi run py-test`, `pixi run cpp-test`.

## If you want CI back

The removed workflows are recoverable from git history:

```sh
git log --diff-filter=D --name-only -- .github/workflows/
git show <commit>^:.github/workflows/ci.yml
```

Bring them back one at a time, and make the pyo3 config generation an explicit
step before any `cargo` invocation that touches the workspace.
